leftEvidence.title: Ziklag is burned and David strengthens himself

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David’s company finds the city burned and families taken, weeps, turns bitter, while David strengthens himself in the LORD, inquires, and receives an Egyptian guide.
points.right: David strikes the Amalekites, recovers every person and possession, rejects exclusion of those who stayed with the baggage, and sends gifts to Judah’s elders.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places collapse turns toward pursuit through inquiry and unexpected help inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places restoration becomes a distribution rule and renewed relation with Judah inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Samuel 30:1–15 and 1 Samuel 30:16–31 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Philistine Brink and Recovery” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Recovery becomes a rule about sharing

payload.tension: 1 Samuel 30:1–15 foregrounds collapse turns toward pursuit through inquiry and unexpected help; 1 Samuel 30:16–31 foregrounds restoration becomes a distribution rule and renewed relation with Judah. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
